newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS - FX vols soar as dlr jump above 114 yen.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - FX vols soar as dlr jump above 114 yen.

text.p: Implied volatilities for dollar/yen options were sharply higher in late U.S. trade as the dollar jumped above 114.00 yen, dealers said.

"Spot has moved a lot higher and people didn't really have strike prices at these levels in their books," said Kyoko Hiramatsu, senior trader at Bank of Yokohama in New York. "Demand for these higher strikes will keep volatilities bid for a while."
Traders added that tension ahead of Friday's U.S. employment report and next week's U.S. presidential elections would also underpin volatilities.
One-month dollar/yen implied volatility rose a full point from late Friday levels to 8.1/8.3 percent.
One-year, which has been in demand lately, also rose nearly a full point to 10.0/10.2 percent.
"That's a lot for one-year," said a U.S. bank trader in New York, referring to the impact of the rise on actual premiums.
He said the yen volatility curve was likely to remain steep in the near term as the back end would be resilient even when the front end recoils after a corrective pull-back in the spot dollar.
Risk reversals, which reflect pricing skew for puts and calls, shifted toward yen puts slowly but steadily. One-month 25-delta was quoted at around par.
Traders, however, cautioned that flips toward yen puts in the one-month area this year had usually been followed shortly by an end to the dollar's bull cycle.
In fact, some Japanese exporters were seen buying low-delta yen calls in the back end for long-term protection.
The sickly yen was weaker against most major currencies, prompting a barrage of stop-loss orders in both spot and options, traders said.
Spot mark/yen climbed above 75.00 yen for the first time since February 1993. Implied volatility for one-month mark/yen rose nearly half a point to 6.9/7.2 percent.
Dollar/mark implied volatilities were also slightly firmer, as the dollar tested lows around 1.5170 marks.
Still, traders said activity was slow because dollar/mark had been the least interesting sector of the market in the past few weeks, merely reacting to activity in the crosses.
One-month dollar/mark volatility was up a tenth of a point from late Friday at 7.0/7.2 percent, while one-year stood steady at 7.9/8.0 percent.
Elsewhere, sterling volatilities remained firm as cable tested fresh highs above $1.6140. One-month cable gained half a point to 6.3/6.6 percent.
